 :JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.5,00,000/ for the damages caused to the lorry bearing No.KA438179 in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 07062020 at about 9.15 a.m., the Petitioner's lorry bearing No.KA43 8179 was carrying 40 cement electrical poles from Bengaluru to P.K.S.Prestress Concrete Products, situated at Survey No.265, PIPB Road, Doddabasthi.

The driver of the lorry has reached and parked the lorry on the left side of the road NH766 between Halladamada Cross  Raghavapura and went for nature call, at that time,
the lorry bearing No.KL 11BJ1511 driven by its driver came from Mysore side and dashed against the lorry which was parked on the left side of the road.

Due to the impact, the Cement electrical poles loaded in the lorry bearing No.KA438179 were damaged and the right side back portion of the lorry was also damaged, one rear side tyre of the lorry was burst (broken) and other parts was also damaged.
The accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The cost of manufacture of one cement electrical pole is Rs.4,700/.
In the said accident ten cement electrical poles have been damagedair crack and three cement electrical poles were completely damaged,
As such, the Petitioner had sustained loss of Rs.61,100/.
For repairing the said vehicle, the Petitioner has spent Rs.50,000/.
Further the lorry was kept idle for 10 days in the workshop for repairs amounting to Rs.80,000/.

The said accident is occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the said Lorry bearing No.KL11BJ1511 by its driver and the Respondent No.1 being the RC owner and the Respondent No. 2 being the insurer of the Lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 did not appear before the court.
Hence, he was placed Exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its objections.

Further it contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident and the insured vehicle does not had permit and fitness certificate.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

On these grounds, the Respondent No.
2 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my Learned predecessor in office has framed the Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that on 08.06.2020 at about 9.15 a.m., when the driver parked the lory bearing Reg.No.KA 438179 NH766 between Hallada Medahalli cross, Raghavapura, near Nursery, Gundlapet Taluk, Chamarajanaar District, at that time, a lorry bearing Reg.No.KL11BJ 1511 its driver drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the Petitioner's Lorry and caused damages to the same?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation ?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award ?

5. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Special Power of Attorney holder of the Petitioner has been examined as P.W.1 and got marked 9 documents as Ex.P.1 to P.9 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 got examined its Assistant Manager as RW.1 and got marked 5 documents as Ex.R.1 to 5. and closed its side evidence.
6. I have heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents and perused the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record.

7. My answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 8. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that the lorry bearing No.KA438179 got damaged in the Motor Vehicle accident that occurred on 08062020 at about 9.15 a.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing Regn. No.KL11BJ1511.

sentences.text: Moreover, after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Chargesheet against the driver of the offending Lorry.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the Petitioner has proved that the accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Lorry and in the said accident, the lorry was damaged.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
17. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Lorry by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
According to the Petitioner, in the said accident, the lorry was damaged.
In order to prove the said fact, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.7, P.8 and Ex.P.9.

Upon going through Ex.P.3 i.e., IMV Report shows that, on an examination, the lorry bearing No.KA438179 was found rear side tyre was burst and damages found on the right side tale lamp, tale lamp guard and right side backside body got damaged.
Upon going through Ex.P.7 i.e., Spot Mahazar wherein the concerned I.O at the time of drawing mahazar had stated that 3 electric poles have been broken out of total 40 electric poles.
Except the broken poles other electric poles have been handed over to the owners of the said electric poles.
PW.1 has also produced Ex.P.8 i.e., Tax invoice/credit bill in respect of the repair charges.
In order to prove the said Ex.P.8, PW.1 has not examined the author of the said document.
Further, PW.1 has not produced any receipt to show that he has paid the said amount which was mentioned in Ex.P.8.
Further, it is pertinent to note here that Petitioner has not conducted any survey of his lorry in respect of the damages and the electric poles.
Further, in the cross examination of PW.1 he has admitted that, he has not produced survey report and OD claim certificate.
Further he deposed that since he has not claimed OD claim, he has not produced the said document.
Further in the cross examination he deposed that he can produce receipt for the payment of bill which was shown in Ex.P.8.
But, subsequently also he has not produced the said receipt.
Further, he admitted that he has no knowledge about the said matter.

However, the Charge sheet i.e., Ex.P.5 shows that in the said accident 3 electric poles were broken and Petitioner has sustained loss of Rs.19,500/.
In the petition, it is stated that the lorry was kept idle for 10 days in the workshop for repairs.
However, there is no document produced to show that lorry was kept idle for 10 days.

Moreover,
there is no cogent evidence is produced in this regard.

Hence, by considering all these aspects, in the absence of survey report and oral evidence of author of Ex.P.8 and also non production of Receipt in respect of the payment of bill shown in the Ex.P.8 and by considering the damages found in the IMV Report and the loss in respect of electric poles shown in the charge sheet it would be lawful to notionally hold that the Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.50,000/ in this regard.

18. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Lorry bearing No.KL11 BJ1511.
The Petition shows the Policy is in force as on the date of accident.

sentences.text: Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
19. Point No. 3 : In view of my findings on Points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No. 1 and 2 U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.50,000/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, since the same is meager is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs. 1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
